Dear Mzansi Lending hiring team,

Mzansi Lending is adding AI to its customer operations and needs someone to build internal tools from prototype to production. That is the work I do now. At Ubuntu Retail Analytics I built an internal FastAPI service that uses the Claude API to summarise customer reviews. It is used by 3 teams, and it reflects how I like to work: taking a feature from idea to deployment. A similar approach could help your operations team work through messages from small-business customers more quickly.

I also check whether LLM output is any good. I prototyped a support ticket classifier that routes support emails with an LLM and evaluated it on 50 labelled emails, where it reached 84% accuracy. Routing and triage map closely onto customer operations, and I want to apply more rigorous evaluation at production scale.

Underneath the AI work, I build data infrastructure. I maintain 12 Python ETL pipelines using Airflow and PostgreSQL. I cut a nightly sales-report runtime from 3 hours to 40 minutes by rewriting SQL queries and adding indexes. I also raised pipeline test coverage from 20% to 65% with pytest. Before that, as a Data Intern at Khanya Insurance, I cleaned and analysed claims data in pandas and built Power BI reports for the claims team. That work is close to the kind of operational records a lender relies on.

My Docker experience is basic, and I expect to deepen it quickly on your stack. I'm based in Johannesburg, so the hybrid schedule suits me. I speak isiZulu and Sesotho as well as English, which could be useful when building tools for an operations team that serves customers across South Africa.

I'd welcome the chance to talk about what your operations team needs first.

Lerato Dlamini

Dear Savanna Health AI hiring team,

Your Senior Machine Learning Engineer post calls for strong Python and SQL and hands-on LLM work in health AI. I'm applying speculatively. I don't meet the senior bar: I have about two years' experience and no PyTorch model training, Kubernetes or AWS work. I'd like to be considered for any junior or mid-level LLM application or data engineering role on your team.

Python and SQL are my daily work. As a Junior Data Engineer at Ubuntu Retail Analytics, I built and maintain 12 Python ETL pipelines on Airflow and PostgreSQL. I also cut the nightly sales-report runtime from 3 hours to 40 minutes by rewriting SQL queries and adding indexes.

On the LLM side, I've shipped an LLM-powered internal tool and prototyped an LLM classifier. The tool is a FastAPI service that uses the Claude API to summarise customer reviews, and 3 teams use it. The classifier routes support emails and reached 84% accuracy on 50 labelled emails. Measuring LLM output against labelled data is an approach I would bring to health applications. I'm keen to learn retrieval-augmented generation, which I haven't built yet.

Health data calls for careful handling, and that is where my testing discipline is relevant. I wrote pytest suites for my pipelines, raising coverage from 20% to 65%. Before that, as a Data Intern at Khanya Insurance, I cleaned and analysed claims data in pandas and built Power BI reports for the claims team. That is the closest I've come to the healthcare data your post lists as an advantage.

I'm based in Johannesburg, so your remote South Africa setup suits me. If a role at my level opens, I'd welcome a conversation.

Lerato Dlamini

dealbreakers: Requires US work authorization without sponsorship; CV shows a South Africa-based candidate with no stated US work authorization
Requires on-site work in Austin, Texas 5 days a week; candidate is based in Johannesburg
checker_unsupported: "it is now used by 3 teams outside my own": the CV says only "used by 3 teams" and does not say whether they are outside her own team. Drop "outside my own".

"I'd welcome the chance to own reporting end-to-end again, from the SQL query to the finished Power BI dashboard": "again" implies she previously owned reporting from SQL query to dashboard. The CV's Khanya entry mentions only pandas cleaning and Power BI reports, not SQL. Reword, e.g. "I'd welcome the chance to build dashboards myself again, as I did with Power BI at Khanya."

"Both roles have depended on working closely with the people who use the data": the CV shows she produced reports and pipelines for the claims and BI teams, but it never describes close collaboration with users. Soften this, or back it with a concrete example she can confirm.

Dear Hiring Team,

At Ubuntu Retail Analytics, I cut our nightly sales-report runtime from 3 hours to 40 minutes by rewriting SQL queries and adding indexes. I'd bring that same focus on fast, reliable reporting to Lone Star Logistics as a Data Analyst.

Since February 2024 I've worked as a Junior Data Engineer. I built and maintain 12 Python ETL pipelines (Airflow, PostgreSQL) that feed the BI team's dashboards. I also wrote pytest suites for them, raising coverage from 20% to 65%. Before that, as a Data Intern at Khanya Insurance, I cleaned and analysed claims data in pandas and built Power BI reports for the claims team.

Both roles have depended on working closely with the people who use the data. At Khanya I produced Power BI reports for the claims team. At Ubuntu my pipelines supply the BI team's dashboards. I also built an internal FastAPI service that uses the Claude API to summarise customer reviews, and it is now used by 3 teams outside my own.

In my current role I supply dashboards rather than build them. I'd welcome the chance to own reporting end-to-end again, from the SQL query to the finished Power BI dashboard. I don't yet have logistics or supply-chain experience. However, I've already worked with retail sales and insurance claims data, and I'm keen to learn the metrics that matter in your operations.

I hold a BSc in Computer Science from the University of Johannesburg (2023) and have two years of hands-on Python and SQL work. I'd be glad to discuss how I could help your team turn logistics data into clear, timely reporting.

Kind regards,
Lerato Dlamini

Dear [Hiring Manager],

CloudNine Systems is hiring a Platform Engineer to keep production infrastructure reliable and to write the Python or Go that supports it. I'm a Python developer with 2 years' experience building data pipelines and LLM-powered tools, and I want to move toward platform work.

Since February 2024 I've been a Junior Data Engineer at Ubuntu Retail Analytics. There I built and maintain 12 Python ETL pipelines on Airflow and PostgreSQL that feed the BI team's dashboards. Keeping those pipelines dependable has made me care about what runs overnight. I cut the nightly sales-report runtime from 3 hours to 40 minutes by rewriting SQL queries and adding indexes. I also wrote pytest suites that raised the pipelines' test coverage from 20% to 65%.

I'm comfortable taking a feature from idea to deployment. For example, I built an internal FastAPI service that uses the Claude API to summarise customer reviews, and 3 teams now use it. I use Git and have basic Docker experience.

I should be direct about the gaps. I haven't run Kubernetes in production, and I haven't yet worked with Terraform, AWS or an on-call rotation. My strengths are Python, automation, and making existing systems faster and better tested. I'd bring those to learning your stack. I'm based in Johannesburg and have worked in Cape Town before, as a Data Intern at Khanya Insurance.

If you see a fit for someone with my background, or a more junior platform role opens up, I'd welcome a conversation.

Kind regards,
Lerato Dlamini
